NFL Report — five-factor system

Aaron Brown’s demonstration NFL betting system (Wilmott magazine): the replicated 2015 & 2016 reports, plus seven seasons generated from raw data.

Replication (2015 & 2016): every published bet and result is reproduced — 175 bets, 92–79 (53.8%), +5.1 units at full juice. System # matches 532/534 games (the 2 misses are rounding ties in the published power column). 7 further seasons (2019–20 to 2025–26) are generated from raw data by the same engine: 553 bets, 267–269 (49.8%), -28.9 units.

Factor diagnostics

Brown’s own monitoring tools, rebuilt. Marginal contribution charges a factor only on close calls its vote alone decided: on a bet made at exactly ±3 every aligned factor earns the result, and on a near-miss at ±2 every opposing factor earns the opposite of what the blocked bet would have done. This accounting reproduces the published Table 3 values for 2015 and 2016 exactly.

Standalone success treats each factor as its own betting rule over all games: the share of its votes that cover the spread. Brown’s bar for a useful factor was 52% (green); below 48% is red.

How the system works

Five binary factors each vote +1 (home), −1 (away) or 0. Their sum is the System #; the model bets home at +3 or more, away at −3 or less, and otherwise passes.

  1. Power / over-reaction — back the team the betting line has moved against relative to slow-moving power ratings; line moves overshoot.
  2. Turnover, home (LGT) — back a home team that gave the ball away last game; turnovers are mostly luck and the line over-corrects.
  3. Turnover, away — the same logic for the away team.
  4. Hunger, home (STDC) — back a home team that has been failing to cover; bookmakers like every team to cover about half the time.
  5. Hunger, away — the same logic for the away team.

Column key: LGT last-game net giveaways · STDC net covers season to date (negative = hungry) · Pwr power rating in points · Line home spread (negative = home favoured).
